public_rationale: The research documents persistent failures, task-dependent performance, and useful successes. It does not establish that dependable performance was rare across generative AI's ordinary uses. Counting selected failures would overstate the evidence; treating productivity gains as general reliability would also overstate it.
limitations: The evidence covers selected language and image tasks rather than the full range of uses.
Some evaluated models predate those available at publication.
The conclusion is sensitive to undefined task weights and reliability standards.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Statistical approximation through generative AI is rarely reliable.

statement.excerpt: Statistical approximation through generative AI is rarely reliable.
statement.document_title: Where’s Waldo? The Elephant in the Room

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that generative AI seldom performs dependably across its ordinary uses. Dependability means consistently meeting the task's requirements, not never making an error.
Marcus supplies neither a numerical meaning of 'rarely' nor a distribution of tasks. I do not invent either.

The target is the state of generative AI at publication. There is no regular reporting cycle or stated beginning, so the period has an unspecified start and ends on the post date. Earlier evaluations of relevant systems are admissible; experiments need not have occurred in January.
Selected failures establish limitations, while selected successes establish capabilities. Neither alone establishes how common dependable performance is.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evaluations of systems available at publication show that dependable performance is uncommon across ordinary uses, with results robust to reasonable choices of tasks and reliability standards.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evaluations of those systems show that dependable performance is common across ordinary uses, with results robust to reasonable choices of tasks and reliability standards.

Our results show that ChatGPT substantially raises average productivity: time taken

evidence.explanation: The writing experiment documents useful performance and improved average quality. It is material counterweight to a failure-only account, but productivity gains do not establish dependable performance across uses.
